differentiator","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"After sunset, rural areas with vegetation and soil moisture lose substantial heat through evapotranspiration and dew formation, converting sensible heat to latent heat that does not warm the air. Urban impervious surfaces have a severe moisture deficit, so this latent heat pathway is largely unavailable. All nocturnal urban cooling must proceed through sensible heat flux and longwave radiation, which are less efficient because the urban surface cannot evaporate. The result is a slower cooling rate in the city and a persistent nighttime temperature excess.
